summary.text: A 56-year-old man had non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy for 6 years on guideline directed medical therapy, with symptomatic heart failure (NYHA III) and a wide QRS with LBBB pattern. A CRT-D was implanted.

Two years later he was admitted with palpitation, with AV node ablation and a CRT-D change to VVI mode for supraventricular tachycardia episodes. Three more admissions followed for ventricular fibrillation episodes and ICD shocks, and mexiletine was initiated.

Two years ago he had nine admissions in ten months with dyspnea and decompensated heart failure despite optimal GDMT, treated with furosemide and milrinone. Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily was initiated and up-titrated to the maximum tolerated dose without hypotension or worsening renal function, with no decompensation hospitalization in the recent fifteen months.

summary.text: A 30-year-old man had dilated cardiomyopathy for 4 years with an ICD-VR. On tolerated heart failure therapy he had three admissions with nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain and diarrhea; endoscopy showed erythematous gastritis and erosive duodenitis, and an inotrope was given for hypotension and cardiogenic shock.

Two weeks after the last hospitalization he came with heart failure symptoms, INTERMACS profile 3 and decreased urine output. Norepinephrine was started and several trials of inotrope discontinuation were unsuccessful.

Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily was initiated at a systolic blood pressure of about 100 mm Hg, and norepinephrine infusion was tapered off. No adverse side effects occurred, up-titration was done at follow-up visits, and there was no admission during 18 months.

summary.text: A 35-year-old man had dilated cardiomyopathy treated for 3 years, with an ICD-VR. He had three hospitalizations for heart failure decompensation in the second year despite optimal tolerable GDMT; in the third admission norepinephrine was given for hypotension and cardiogenic shock.

A few days later blood pressure rose and norepinephrine was withdrawn, after which elevated bilirubin and reduced urine output developed with INTERMACS 3. Milrinone was started and he did well on it, but signs of organ hypo-perfusion returned on reducing it.

Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily was started at a systolic pressure of about 100 mm Hg. A few days later milrinone was discontinued without organ damage signs and he was discharged in good condition without side effects. Over 1 year of follow-up there was no heart failure admission except one two weeks after ARNI initiation.

summary.text: A 24-year-old man had dilated cardiomyopathy diagnosed one year earlier. At his first admission with decompensation symptoms on optimal tolerable GDMT, norepinephrine and milrinone were administered, and the inotropes could not be discontinued because of deteriorating congestive symptoms and a low output state.

Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily was initiated once systolic blood pressure reached approximately 100 mm Hg. A few days later his condition improved without S/V side effects, the inotropes were discontinued and he was discharged in good condition. About one year later he had acceptable function without heart failure hospitalization.
